[MATH: {y = − 3x − 5; 5y = 2x − 8]

The solution to the given system of equations is [MATH: (x, y).] What is the value of [MATH: x - y?]

sections.normalized_html:
Since the first equation is already solved for [MATH: y,] we can substitute [MATH: y = -3x - 5] into the second equation and solve:

[MATH: 5y|= 2x − 8; 5(− 3x − 5)|= 2x − 8; − 15x − 25|= 2x − 8; − 15x − 2x|= − 8 + 25; − 17x|= 17; x|= − 1]

Now, using the equality [MATH: y = -3x - 5,] we have

[MATH: x − y|= x − (− 3x − 5); = x + 3x + 5; = 4x + 5]

Hence,

[MATH: x − y|= 4x + 5; = 4(− 1) + 5; = − 4 + 5; = 1]
